prompts.inverts-signs:
Use case: AI-illustrated hobby guide that helps a beginner reef-aquarium keeper recognise what is wrong with their shrimp, crabs, snails, urchins and starfish.
LOOK: every cell is an ORDINARY, CANDID PHONE SNAPSHOT a hobbyist took through the front glass of their own home reef tank, the way the problem really looks in a typical aquarium. NOT a studio shot, NOT a posed nature-documentary macro, NOT a stock photo. The animal is NOT centred or posed: it is off to one side, often partly behind live rock or a coral frag, seen slightly off-angle through the glass. Faint reflections and a light smudge or film of algae on the glass; patchy pink coralline and a little green/brown film algae on the live rock; sand with bits of detritus and uneaten food; uneven blue-white LED reef lighting with a blue cast and some areas in shadow; mild phone-camera softness, a little noise, imperfect focus at the edges. Show the whole situation (posture, surroundings, other animals) as it really looks in a tank, NOT one perfect painted mark on an otherwise perfect healthy animal. Still, the problem in each cell must be clearly recognisable to a novice at thumbnail size. Photographic and believable, not gory. Not cartoons, icons, illustrations, 3D renders or typography. No people, hands or tools. Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, labels, logos, watermarks, arrows or symbols anywhere in the image.
STRICT CONTACT SHEET for cropping into twelve separate pictures: exactly FOUR equal-width columns and THREE equal-height rows, twelve equal square cells covering the complete image edge to edge. No gutters, no borders, no outer margin. Every cell is its own separate tank snapshot with its own background. Nothing crosses a cell boundary; keep the main subject inside the central 85 percent of its cell. Never put a cell's subject into another cell. Follow the exact row-major order below.
Animals (draw each one exactly as named): SKUNK CLEANER SHRIMP = Lysmata amboinensis, a red-orange back split by one white stripe from head to tail, long white antennae, yellowish legs. PEPPERMINT SHRIMP = small, translucent pinkish body with thin red stripes. FIRE SHRIMP = deep blood-red with a few white spots and long white antennae. HERMIT CRAB = a small reef hermit (blue-leg or scarlet hermit) living in an empty sea-snail shell. EMERALD CRAB = Mithrax, a small flat bright-green crab with a round body and short claws. TURBO / TROCHUS SNAIL = a grazing sea snail with a cone-shaped, ridged shell. URCHIN = a tuxedo urchin (short spines, blue-black with bands). Exactly the animals each cell names, at a believable small size for a home aquarium.
Row 1 column 1: a SKUNK CLEANER SHRIMP STUCK HALFWAY OUT OF ITS OLD SHELL, lying limp on its side on the sand at the foot of the rock: the cloudy, milky old skin still clinging over its tail and back legs, the shrimp itself pale and soft, legs tangled in the old skin, clearly unable to get free.
Row 1 column 2: an EMPTY SHRIMP MOLT: a complete, hollow, see-through ghost-white cleaner shrimp shell with all its legs and antennae, lying on top of the live rock in the open; it looks exactly like a dead shrimp at first glance, but it is hollow and translucent, split open behind the head. No live shrimp in this cell.
Row 1 column 3: a SKUNK CLEANER SHRIMP whose body has turned MILKY, CLOUDY WHITE and opaque, its red and white colours washed out to a dull chalky pink-white; it sits low and still under a rock ledge, partly in shadow.
Row 1 column 4: the morning after a medicine was dosed: SEVERAL DEAD AND DYING INVERTEBRATES scattered over the sand in front of the rock: a pale curled-up cleaner shrimp on its side, two turbo snails fallen off the glass lying upside down, a hermit crab hanging limp half out of its shell. A healthy fish swims in the background.
Row 2 column 1: a TURBO SNAIL LYING UPSIDE DOWN ON ITS BACK on the sand next to the rock, the shell opening facing up, the foot barely showing; it has clearly fallen off the rock and cannot turn over. A few grains of sand and detritus around it.
Row 2 column 2: a PEPPERMINT SHRIMP perched on the rock, seen from the side, with an obvious LOPSIDED SWOLLEN BULGE on ONE side of its shell just behind the eye, as if a blister or a lump is pushing the side of the head shell outwards; otherwise it looks normal and active.
Row 2 column 3: TWO HERMIT CRABS FIGHTING over one empty snail shell on the sand: claws locked, one hermit dragged half out of its shell with its soft curled pale abdomen showing; a single detached crab leg lying on the sand nearby.
Row 2 column 4: a FIRE SHRIMP that has LOST ITS COLOUR: instead of deep blood-red it has faded to a blotchy, dull pale pink-orange, sitting on bare-ish rock near the back of the tank; a normal bright red fire shrimp would look completely different.
Row 3 column 1: a TUXEDO URCHIN LOSING ITS SPINES: several BALD PATCHES on its body where the spines have dropped off, many loose spines scattered on the rock and sand beneath it, the urchin clinging weakly low on the rock.
Row 3 column 2: a SKUNK CLEANER SHRIMP HIDING deep in a dark crevice of the live rock at feeding time, only its head and folded antennae visible, while uneaten food pellets lie on the sand in front; it looks healthy but is not coming out.
Row 3 column 3: a SKUNK CLEANER SHRIMP perched on the rock that is MISSING TWO WALKING LEGS on one side, with one of its long white antennae broken off short; a fish swims behind; otherwise the shrimp looks normal.
Row 3 column 4: an EMERALD CRAB LYING STILL ON ITS BACK on the open sand, legs curled up over its body, not moving, a hermit crab and a snail nearby.

Row 1 column 1: a SKUNK CLEANER SHRIMP on the rock seen clearly from the side, OBVIOUSLY MISSING LEGS: on the near side only two thin walking legs remain with clear empty gaps where three legs are gone, and one of its two long white antennae is SNAPPED OFF to a short stub; a fish swims behind.

Row 3 column 2: DEAD CRABS after a medicine: two hermit crabs lying limp out of their shells on the sand and an emerald crab dead on its back nearby.
Row 3 column 3: a SKUNK CLEANER SHRIMP standing on the sand in front of the rock, seen side-on and close, with several WALKING LEGS CLEARLY MISSING on the near side (big empty gaps between the remaining legs) and one long antenna broken short.
Row 3 column 4: an EMERALD CRAB on the rock MISSING ONE OF ITS TWO CLAWS: one claw normal, on the other side only a small stump; one walking leg missing too.

review.method: Every sheet opened and every crop checked for the right animal, the problem visible at thumbnail size, the ordinary home-tank snapshot look (off-centre, rock, detritus, glass, blue-white light), nothing crossing cell edges and no text; full-size strips of the borderline crops and a labelled contact image of all crops reviewed (workspace/.openclaw/tmp/fhl-inverts/all-crops.jpg).
review.styleResult: All four sheets came back as candid tank snapshots (animals off-centre, partly behind rock, sand with detritus and food, coralline and film algae, glass edges/reflections, blue-white lighting). No studio look, no text artifacts, no cell-edge crossings.
repairs: inverts-repair (one mixed 4x3 sheet) retook four cells: sign-shrimp-legs (first take: missing legs not visible; two retakes, the sand take used), cond-failed-molt (first take: shrimp standing upright, read weakly as stuck; retake lies limp on its side with the old skin stuck over its tail), sign-deaths (first take: snails looked upright and alive, dead shrimp tiny; retake has several upturned snails and a larger dead shrimp), sign-other-not-moving (first take: urchin just sitting on the sand; retake lies upside down, mouth side up).

The same sheet added kind-specific cells the three planned sheets had no room for: snail/crab/other deaths, serpent star hiding, urchin + starfish after copper, a crab after acclimation, an emerald crab missing a claw.

weakCells.sign-shrimp-legs (retake): missing legs shown as a shrimp with only two walking legs and one antenna; no visible stumps. Readable, not dramatic.
weakCells.sign-crab-legs: the missing claw is a small stump on the far side; the one remaining claw is obvious.
weakCells.cond-crab-acclimation: the crab is small in the frame next to the glass under the floating bag.
weakCells.sign-crab-deaths: the emerald crab on its back is clear; the two hermits still sit in their shells.
weakCells.sign-snail-unclear / sign-crab-unclear: "just seems off" has nothing visible by nature: a snail sitting still on the glass, a hermit withdrawn in its shell by uneaten food.
weakCells.sign-bulge: the bopyrid bulge sits high on the head shell rather than low on the side; still clearly a lump behind the head.
weakCells.cond-flipped: the trochus sits opening-up with its foot stretched upwards (on its back, trying to turn), rather than lying flat on its side.
